issue_context.title: SET timestamp=default is setting value to null
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)
```sql
SET timestamp=default;
select @@timestamp;
```
### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
```sql
mysql> set timestamp = default;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> select @@timestamp;
+-------------------+
| @@timestamp       |
+-------------------+
| 1635956082.324848 |
+-------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```
### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
```sql
mysql> set timestamp = default;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> select @@timestamp;
+-------------+
| @@timestamp |
+-------------+
|             |
+-------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```
### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

```sql
+-------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Variable_name           | Value                                                                    |
+-------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| innodb_version          | 5.6.25                                                                   |
| protocol_version        | 10                                                                       |
| tidb_analyze_version    | 2                                                                        |
| tidb_row_format_version | 2                                                                        |
| tls_version             | TLSv1,TLSv1.1,TLSv1.2                                                    |
| version                 | 5.7.25-TiDB-v5.2.1                                                       |
| version_comment         | TiDB Server (Apache License 2.0) Community Edition, MySQL 5.7 compatible |
| version_compile_machine | x86_64                                                                   |
| version_compile_os      | osx10.8                                                                  |
+-------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
comments: This is a good first issue for contributors. It requires a `GetSession` function to be added for the `Timestamp` system variable to read the internal timestamp which is used by temporal functions. See https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/28072 for a previous example that is similar.

> This is a good first issue for contributors. It requires a `GetSession` function to be added for the `Timestamp` system variable to read the internal timestamp which is used by temporal functions. See #28072 for a previous example that is similar.

@morgo I got your point, could you please tell me where can I find such temporal function in TiDB that provides internal timestamp

Temporal functions like `NOW()` call this function: https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/9bbc7ad74a540d61a1d47f7212bd0f9cd0244b76/expression/helper.go#L135-L167

So the GetSession func would have to have similar logic - if there is a value for s.systems[Timestamp] use it, otherwise use s.StmtCtx.GetOrStoreStmtCache..
Please check whether the issue should be labeled with 'affects-x.y' or 'fixes-x.y.z', and then remove 'needs-more-info' label.

review_comments: Please also check `select now();select now();` since it should also return the static time according to the set timestamp and should not reset for the second case (seems correct, but better be clear by adding it in the test as well).
